summary: Telescope Hill's 1918 fire tower near Selden was removed in 1960; the summit now carries radio facilities, and sources disagree on who owns the land.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1960; the summit now hosts radio tower facilities

events.note: Erected in the fall of 1918 as the first of Long Island's fire lookouts
First fire observer Al Lucas, who served two years; tower in operation March 1919
120 fires reported between March 17 and June 15, 1919
Frank Forsyth on duty (spelled Forsythe in the 1938 item)
State ended support for fire towers on Long Island after the 1959 season; lookout services abandoned
Transfer of title to Suffolk County arranged, per Forest Lookouts

corrections.why: Wikipedia gives the hill at 334 feet (102 m), the highest point in the Town of Brookhaven; the record's 98.5 m is lower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives 1918; Wikipedia says the first tower was constructed in fall 1918 and went into operation March 1919. Story uses 1918 for construction and 1919 for operation.
FFLOS and Wikipedia both date the closure to after the 1959 season and the removal to 1960.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved, so left out of facts: height (Wikipedia 60-ft Aermotor vs 69 ft in the 1918 Echo item, quoted by Forest Lookouts); current land owner (FFLOS says privately held, Forest Lookouts says title transfer to Suffolk County was arranged), so access is unset. No source describes public access or what remains on the site. Summit radio facilities come from Wikipedia, undated. Record elevation 98.5 m differs from Wikipedia's 102 m for the hill. No photos fetched.
